[LCSP.4.5] **String-typed series are rejected.** A `series` declared
over a `String`-typed slot, on any backing that stores raw sample
values, is a compile error under `constspace`
(`DS_VALIDATE_RT_STRING_SERIES`).

The reason is the absorb path, not the window. A value-storing backing
owns its samples and copies each one on absorb, so a `String` element
type allocates **per absorbed sample**, at pump time, for the life of
the series — and frees on eviction. That is a steady-state allocation,
which is the one thing `constspace` guarantees against ([LCSP.2]).

**Which backings store values is the load-bearing part.** They
are `SeriesBackendRingBuffer`, `SeriesBackendFifoDeque` and `SeriesBackendReservoir`, and those are exactly the backings a
`String`-typed slot can reach: per [LSER.17.2] the only aggregations
applicable to `String` are `count`, `count_distinct`, `count_of`,
`contains`, `first` and `last`; per [LSER.18.1] those route to
`SeriesBackendWelfordEwma` / `SeriesBackendRingBuffer` / `SeriesBackendReservoir` and `SeriesBackendWelfordEwma` / `SeriesBackendFifoDeque`, with the exact sliding
set and table forms carried on `SeriesBackendRingBuffer`. `SeriesBackendWelfordEwma` holds running
accumulators rather than samples, so it does not copy.

The obligation is on the property, and an implementation that checks a
fixed list satisfies it only while the list is complete.

This is a distinct axis from [LNLS.3.11] /
`DS_VALIDATE_RT_SERIES_UNBOUNDED`, which bound the *sample count*. A
`String` series with a perfectly bounded window still allocates once
per sample, so a capacity bound does not rescue it and the two checks
do not subsume each other.

The same allocation occurs under `realtime`, which carries the
constant-space concern as one of its three ([LCSP.1.1]) and states the
zero-steady-state-allocation obligation at [RTCT.12.4]; the rejection
applies there for the same reason, and is where the diagnostic's name
comes from.
